'''Rostislav Ivanovich Grigorchuk''' ({{langx|ru|Ростислав Иванович Григорчук}}; {{langx|uk|Ростисла́в Iва́нович Григорчу́к}}; b. February 23, 1953) is a mathematician working in different areas of mathematics including [[group theory]], [[dynamical systems]], [[geometry]] and [[computer science]]. He holds the rank of [[Professors in the United States|Distinguished Professor]] in the Mathematics Department of [[Texas A&M University]]. Grigorchuk is particularly well known for having constructed, in a 1984 paper,<ref name="g1"/> the first example of a [[finitely generated group]] of intermediate [[growth rate (group theory)|growth]], thus answering an important problem posed by [[John Milnor]] in 1968. This group is now known as the [[Grigorchuk group]]<ref name="DH">Pierre de la Harpe. ''Topics in geometric group theory.'' Chicago Lectures in Mathematics. University of Chicago Press, Chicago. {{isbn|0-226-31719-6}}</ref><ref>[[Laurent Bartholdi]]. ''The growth of Grigorchuk's torsion group.'' International Mathematics Research Notices,  1998, no. 20, pp. 1049-1054</ref><ref>Tullio Ceccherini-Silberstein, Antonio Machì, and Fabio Scarabotti. ''The Grigorchuk group of intermediate growth.'' [[Rendiconti del Circolo Matematico di Palermo]] (2), vol. 50 (2001), no. 1, pp. 67-102</ref><ref>Yu. G. Leonov. ''On a lower bound for the growth function of the Grigorchuk group.'' (in Russian).  Matematicheskie Zametki, vol. 67 (2000), no. 3, pp. 475-477; translation in: Mathematical Notes, vol. 67 (2000), no. 3-4, pp. 403-405</ref><ref>Roman Muchnik, and [[Igor Pak]]. ''Percolation on Grigorchuk groups.'' Communications in Algebra, vol. 29 (2001), no. 2, pp. 661-671.</ref>  and it is one of the important objects studied in [[geometric group theory]], particularly in the study of branch groups, automaton groups and [[iterated monodromy group]]s. Grigorchuk is one of the pioneers of asymptotic group theory as well as of the theory of dynamically defined groups. He introduced the notion of branch groups<ref>Grigorchuk R. I.''Just infinite branch groups. New horizons in pro-p groups.''Progr. Math., 184, Birkhäuser Boston, Boston, MA, 2000, 121–179.</ref><ref>Bartholdi, Laurent; Grigorchuk, Rostislav I.; Šuniḱ, Zoran.''Branch groups. Handbook of algebra.''Vol. 3, 989–1112, Handb. Algebr., 3, Elsevier/North-Holland, Amsterdam, 2003.</ref><ref>Grigorchuk Rostislav.''Solved and unsolved problems around one group. Infinite groups: geometric, combinatorial and dynamical aspects.''117–218, Progr. Math., 248, Birkhäuser, Basel, 2005.</ref><ref>de la Harpe, Pierre.''Topics in geometric group theory. (English summary).''Chicago Lectures in Mathematics. University of Chicago Press, Chicago, IL, 2000.</ref> and developed the foundations of the related theory. Grigorchuk, together with his collaborators and students, initiated the theory of groups generated by finite Mealy type automata,<ref>Grigorchuk R. I.; Nekrashevich, V. V.; Sushchanskiĭ, V. I.''Automata, dynamical systems, and groups. (Russian).''Tr. Mat. Inst. Steklova 231 (2000), Din. Sist., Avtom. i Beskon. Gruppy, 134–214; translation in Proc. Steklov Inst. Math. 2000, no. 4(231), 128–203.</ref><ref>Bondarenko, Ievgen; Grigorchuk, Rostislav; Kravchenko, Rostyslav; Muntyan, Yevgen; Nekrashevych, Volodymyr; Savchuk, Dmytro; Šunić, Zoran.''On classification of groups generated by 3-state automata over a 2-letter alphabet.''Algebra Discrete Math. 2008, no. 1, 1–163.</ref><ref>Ceccherini-Silberstein, Tullio and Coornaert, Michel.''Cellular automata and groups.''Springer Monographs in Mathematics. Springer-Verlag, Berlin, 2010.</ref> interpreted them as groups of [[fractal]] type,<ref>Bartholdi, Laurent; Grigorchuk, Rostislav; Nekrashevych, Volodymyr.''From fractal groups to fractal sets.''Fractals in Graz 2001, 25–118, Trends Math., Birkhäuser, Basel, 2003.</ref><ref>Grigorchuk, Rostislav; Nekrashevych, Volodymyr; Šunić, Zoran.''From self-similar groups to self-similar sets and spectra. Fractal geometry and stochastics V.'' 175–207, Progr. Probab., 70, Birkhäuser/Springer, Cham, 2015.</ref> developed the theory of groups acting on rooted trees,<ref>Grigorchuk R. I.''Some problems of the dynamics of group actions on rooted trees. (Russian)''Tr. Mat. Inst. Steklova 273 (2011).</ref> and found numerous applications<ref>Grigorchuk, Rostislav; Šunić, Zoran.''Self-similarity and branching in group theory.''Groups St. Andrews 2005. Vol. 1, 36–95, London Math. Soc. Lecture Note Ser., 339, Cambridge Univ. Press, Cambridge, 2007.</ref><ref>Nekrashevych, Volodymyr.''Self-similar groups.''Mathematical Surveys and Monographs, 117. American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 2005. xii+231 pp</ref><ref>Grigorchuk, Rostislav; Nekrashevych, Volodymyr.''Self-similar groups, operator algebras and Schur complement.''J. Mod. Dyn. 1 (2007), no. 3, 323–370.</ref> of these groups in various fields of mathematics including [[functional analysis]], [[topology]], [[spectral graph theory]], [[dynamical systems]] and [[ergodic theory]].

==Biographical data==

Grigorchuk was born on February 23, 1953, in [[Ternopil Oblast]], now [[Ukraine]] (in 1953 part of the [[USSR]]).<ref name="bio"/>
He received his undergraduate degree in 1975 from [[Moscow State University]].
He obtained a PhD (Candidate of Science) in Mathematics in 1978, also from [[Moscow State University]], where his thesis advisor was [[Anatoly Mikhailovich Stepin|Anatoly M. Stepin]]. Grigorchuk received a habilitation (Doctor of Science) degree in Mathematics in 1985 at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] in [[Moscow]].<ref name="bio"/> During the 1980s and 1990s, Rostislav Grigorchuk held positions at the [[Moscow State University of Railway Engineering|Moscow State University of Transportation]], and subsequently at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] and [[Moscow State University]].<ref name="bio"/> In 2002 Grigorchuk joined the faculty of [[Texas A&M University]] as a Professor of Mathematics, and he was promoted to the rank of Distinguished Professor in 2008.<ref>[http://www.math.tamu.edu/news/2008pers.html 2008 Personal News], Department of Mathematics, [[Texas A&M University]]. Accessed January 15, 2010.</ref>

Rostislav Grigorchuk gave an invited address at the 1990 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Kyoto]]<ref>R. I. Grigorchuk. ''On growth in group theory.'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Vol. I, II (Kyoto, 1990), pp. 325-338, Math. Soc. Japan, Tokyo, 1991</ref> an AMS Invited Address at the March 2004 meeting of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in Athens, Ohio<ref>[http://e-math.ams.org/amsmtgs/2090_invited.html Spring Central Section Meeting,  Athens, OH, March 26-27, 2004.] [[American Mathematical Society]]. Accessed January 15, 2010.</ref> and a plenary talk at the 2004 Winter Meeting of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.smc.math.ca/Events/winter04/speakers.e 2004 Winter Meeting], [[Canadian Mathematical Society]]. Accessed January 15, 2010.</ref>

Grigorchuk is the Editor-in-Chief of the journal ''"Groups, Geometry and Dynamics"'',<ref>[http://www.math.tamu.edu/journals/ggd/ ''Groups, Geometry and Dynamics'']</ref> published by the [[European Mathematical Society]], and is or was a member of the editorial boards of the journals ''"Mathematical Notes"'',<ref>[http://www.mathnet.ru/php/journal.phtml?jrnid=mzm&wshow=details&option_lang=eng Editorial Board, Mathematical Notes]</ref>  ''"International Journal of Algebra and Computation"'',<ref>[http://www.worldscinet.com/ijac/mkt/editorial.shtml Editorial Board, International Journal of Algebra and Computation]</ref> ''"Journal of Modern Dynamics"'',<ref>[http://www.math.psu.edu/jmd/EditorialBoard.html Editorial Board, Journal of Modern Dynamics]</ref> ''"Geometriae Dedicata"'',<ref>[https://www.springer.com/math/geometry/journal/10711?detailsPage=editorialBoard Editorial Board, Geometriae Dedicata]</ref>  ''"Ukrainian Mathematical Journal"'',<ref>[https://www.springer.com/journal/11253/editors Editorial Board, Ukrainian Mathematical Journal]</ref> ''"Algebra and Discrete Mathematics"'',<ref>[http://adm.lnpu.edu.ua/editorial/index_frame.htm Editorial Board, Algebra and Discrete Mathematics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081121112756/http://adm.lnpu.edu.ua/editorial/index_frame.htm |date=2008-11-21 }}</ref>  ''"Carpathian Mathematical Publications"'',<ref>[https://journals.pnu.edu.ua/index.php/cmp/editorialteam Editorial Board, Carpathian Mathematical Publications]</ref>   ''"Bukovinian Mathematical Journal"'',<ref>[http://bmj.fmi.org.ua/index.php/adm/about/editorialTeam Editorial Board, Bukovinian Mathematical Journal]</ref>  and ''"Matematychni Studii"''.<ref>[http://matstud.org.ua/ojs/index.php/matstud/about/editorialTeam Editorial Board, Matematychni Studii]</ref>

==Mathematical contributions==

Grigorchuk is most well known for having constructed the first example of a finitely generated group of intermediate growth which now bears his name and is called the '''[[Grigorchuk group]]''' (sometimes it is also called the '''first Grigorchuk group''' since Grigorchuk constructed several other groups that are also commonly studied). This group has [[Growth rate (group theory)|growth]] that is faster than polynomial but slower than exponential. Grigorchuk constructed this group in a 1980 paper<ref>R. I. Grigorchuk. ''On Burnside's problem on periodic groups.'' (Russian) Funktsionalnyi Analiz i ego Prilozheniya, vol.  14 (1980), no. 1, pp. 53-54</ref> and proved that it has intermediate growth in a 1984 article.<ref name="g1">R. I. Grigorchuk, ''Degrees of growth of finitely generated groups and the theory of invariant means.'' Izvestiya Akademii Nauk SSSR. Seriya Matematicheskaya. vol. 48 (1984), no. 5, pp. 939-985</ref> This result answered a long-standing open problem posed by [[John Milnor]] in 1968 about the existence of finitely generated groups of intermediate growth. Grigorchuk's group has a number of other remarkable mathematical properties. It is a [[finitely generated group|finitely generated]] infinite [[residually finite group|residually finite]] [[p-group|2-group]] (that is, every element of the group has a finite order which is a power of 2). It is also the first example of a finitely generated group that is [[amenable group|amenable]] but not [[Elementary amenable group|elementary amenable]], thus providing an answer to another long-standing problem, posed by [[Mahlon Day]] in 1957.<ref>Mahlon M. Day. ''Amenable semigroups.'' 
[[Illinois Journal of Mathematics]], vol. 1 (1957), pp. 509-544.</ref> Also Grigorchuk's group is ''"just infinite"'': that is, it is infinite but every proper [[quotient group|quotient]] of this group is finite.<ref name="DH"/>

Grigorchuk's group is a central object in the study of the so-called branch groups and automata groups. These are finitely generated groups of automorphisms of rooted trees that are given by particularly nice recursive descriptions and that have remarkable self-similar properties. The study of branch, automata and self-similar groups has been particularly active in the 1990s and 2000s and a number of unexpected connections with other areas of mathematics have been discovered there, including [[dynamical systems]], [[differential geometry]], [[Galois theory]], [[ergodic theory]], [[random walks]], [[fractal]]s, [[Hecke algebra of a locally compact group|Hecke algebras]],  bounded cohomology, [[functional analysis]], and others. In particular, many of these self-similar groups arise as [[iterated monodromy group]]s of complex polynomials. Important connections have been discovered between the algebraic structure of self-similar groups and the dynamical properties of the polynomials in question, including encoding their [[Julia set]]s.<ref>Volodymyr Nekrashevych. ''Self-similar groups.'' Mathematical Surveys and Monographs, 117. American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 2005. {{isbn|0-8218-3831-8}}</ref>

Much of Grigorchuk's work in the 1990s and 2000s has been on developing the theory of branch, automata and self-similar groups and on exploring these connections. For example, Grigorchuk, with co-authors, obtained a counter-example to the conjecture of [[Michael Atiyah]] about ''L<sup>2</sup>''-betti numbers of closed manifolds.<ref>R. I. Grigorchuk, and A. Zuk. ''The lamplighter group as a group generated by a 2-state automaton, and its spectrum.'' 
Geometriae Dedicata,  vol. 87 (2001), no. 1-3, pp. 209--244.</ref><ref>R. I. Grigorchuk, P. Linnell, T. Schick, and A. Zuk. ''On a question of Atiyah.'' Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I. vol. 331 (2000), no. 9, pp. 663-668.</ref>

Grigorchuk is also known for his contributions to the general theory of [[random walks]] on groups and the theory of [[amenable group]]s, particularly for obtaining in 1980<ref>R. I. Grigorchuk. ''Symmetrical random walks on discrete groups.'' Multicomponent random systems, pp. 285-325, Adv. Probab. Related Topics, 6, Marcel Dekker, New York, 1980; {{isbn|0-8247-6831-0}}</ref> what is commonly known (see for example<ref>R. Ortner, and W. Woess. [http://www.cms.math.ca/cjm/a150010 ''Non-backtracking random walks and cogrowth of graphs.''] [[Canadian Journal of Mathematics]], vol. 59 (2007), no. 4, pp. 828-844</ref><ref>Sam Northshield. ''Quasi-regular graphs, cogrowth, and amenability.'' 
Dynamical systems and differential equations (Wilmington, NC, 2002). Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems, Series A. 2003, suppl., pp. 678-687.</ref><ref>Richard Sharp. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130203014229/http://www.springerlink.com/content/mg7502u8676n521h/|title=''Critical exponents for groups of isometries.''}} [[Geometriae Dedicata]], vol. 125 (2007), pp. 63-74</ref>) as '''Grigorchuk's co-growth criterion of amenability''' for [[finitely generated group]]s.

==Awards and honors==

In 1979 Rostislav Grigorchuk was awarded the [[Moscow Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://mms.mathnet.ru/conc.php Laureates of the Moscow Mathematical Society Prize]</ref>

In 1991 he obtained [[Fulbright Senior Scholarship]],<ref>[https://cies.org/fulbright-scholar-directory?grantee=grigorchuk Fulbright Scholar Directory]</ref> [[Columbia University]], New York.

In 2003 an international [[group theory]] conference in honor of Grigorchuk's 50th birthday was held in [[Gaeta, Italy]].<ref>[http://atlas-conferences.com/cgi-bin/calendar/d/facf89 International Conference on GROUP THEORY: combinatorial, geometric, and dynamical aspects of infinite groups.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101212183003/http://atlas-conferences.com/cgi-bin/calendar/d/facf89 |date=2010-12-12 }}</ref> Special anniversary issues of the ''"International Journal of Algebra and Computation"'',<ref>[http://www.worldscinet.com/cgi-bin/details.cgi?id=jsname:ijac&type=all Preface], International Journal of Algebra and Computation, vol. 15 (2005), no. 5-6, pp. v-vi</ref> the journal ''"Algebra and Discrete Mathematics"''<ref name="bio">[http://adm.luguniv.edu.ua/issues/2003/adm_n4_2003_frame.htm Editorial Statement], Algebra and Discrete Mathematics, (2003), no. 4</ref> and the book ''"Infinite Groups: Geometric, Combinatorial and Dynamical Aspects"''<ref>Bartholdi, L., Ceccherini-Silberstein, T., Smirnova-Nagnibeda, T., Zuk, A.''Infinite Groups: Geometric, Combinatorial and Dynamical Aspects.''</ref>  were dedicated to Grigorchuk's 50th birthday.

In 2009 Grigorchuk R.I. was awarded the Association of Former Students Distinguished Achievement in Research,<ref>[https://dof.tamu.edu/dof/media/PITO-DOF/AFS%20DAA/AFS-DAA-University-Level-All-Winners_1.pdf Recipients of The Association of Former Students Distinguished Achievement Awards University Level]</ref> [[Texas A&M University]].

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-19.</ref>

In 2015 Rostislav Grigorchuk was awarded the AMS [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Seminal Contribution to Research.<ref>[http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=2463 AMS 2015 Leroy P. Steele Prize]</ref>

In 2020 Grigorchuk R.I. received the [[Humboldt Research Award]] by Germany’s [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]].<ref>[https://today.tamu.edu/2020/01/28/mathematician-earns-prestigious-humboldt-research-award/ Laureate of Humboldt Research Award]</ref>
